meta.title: Archived Posts
meta.note: Posts that have rolled off the front of the report. Newest first.

items.headline: Travis Etienne will play his first game for the Saints
items.summary: Running back Travis Etienne sat out the preseason, so Sunday at Detroit will be his first game in a Saints uniform. He grew up in Jennings, Louisiana, and ran for more than 1,000 yards in three of his four seasons with Jacksonville.

items.headline: Volpe's grand slam finishes off a sweep
items.summary: Anthony Volpe hit a grand slam in the seventh inning Thursday night and drove in five runs in a 10-3 win. The Yankees swept all three games from Colorado and are now 84-62.

items.headline: Aaron Judge gets a rest day Thursday
items.summary: Judge is out of the lineup for Thursday night's game against Colorado, with Jasson Dominguez playing right field instead. Manager Aaron Boone had said he would give Judge one day off this week as he works back from the broken rib that kept him out since May.

items.headline: Kamara practices again, but Cam Jordan sits out
items.summary: Alvin Kamara practiced Thursday in a limited way as his sore knee gets better before Sunday's opener at Detroit. Cam Jordan did not practice at all with his hurt hamstring, and tight end Oscar Delp and running back Audric Estime sat out too.

items.headline: Cam Jordan will miss Sunday; Kamara back at practice
items.summary: Coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that Cam Jordan's hurt hamstring will keep him out of the opener at Detroit. Alvin Kamara practiced for the first time since he hurt his knee in August, but he was held to a light workload.

items.headline: Rookie's grand slam lifts Yankees over Colorado
items.summary: Rookie George Lombard Jr. hit the first grand slam of his career Wednesday night as the Yankees won 6-1. Aaron Judge went 2 for 4 for his first hits since coming back from a broken rib.

items.headline: Saints name nine captains for the new season
items.summary: Cam Jordan, Erik McCoy, Justin Reid and Zach Wood are captains again, and five more players earned it for the first time. New starting quarterback Tyler Shough is one of them.

items.headline: Yankees beat Colorado 5-3 in Judge's first game back
items.summary: Aaron Judge played right field Tuesday night for the first time since May and went 0 for 3. Ryan McMahon hit the go-ahead double in the fifth inning, and Cam Schlittler pitched seven strong innings.

items.headline: Aaron Judge plays tonight for the first time since May
items.summary: The Yankees put Judge in the lineup Tuesday against Colorado, batting third and playing right field. He missed 84 games with a cracked rib and last played on May 31.

items.headline: Texas lineman Cole Hutson cannot play right now
items.summary: Coach Steve Sarkisian said Hutson is not eligible because he went to two NFL tryout camps last spring. Texas is appealing to the NCAA, and Hutson has started 23 games for the Longhorns.

items.headline: Sumrall wants a cleaner game from the Gators
items.summary: Coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that his defense was not sharp in the 66-21 win over Florida Atlantic. He also said the bad snaps from his center will get fixed before Campbell visits on Saturday.

items.headline: Florida receiver Eric Singleton may miss Saturday
items.summary: Coach Jon Sumrall said Singleton hurt his ankle in the win over Florida Atlantic and is highly questionable for the Campbell game. Sumrall said the team will not know for sure until later in the week.

items.headline: Aaron Judge is back from the injured list
items.summary: The Yankees activated Judge on Monday night, more than three months after he cracked a rib. He is available for the Colorado series that starts Tuesday at Yankee Stadium.

items.headline: Two Florida players got hurt in the opener
items.summary: Coach Jon Sumrall said receiver Eric Singleton Jr. hurt an ankle and running back Evan Pryor had a sore hip in Saturday's win. Sumrall did not know how bad either one is and will say more on Monday.

items.headline: Longtime Saints radio voice Mike Detillier dies
items.summary: Detillier talked about the Saints and LSU on WWL radio for more than 40 years. He died Sunday at age 65, and the Saints called him a true gentleman.

items.headline: Aaron Judge hits on the field again
items.summary: Judge took batting practice on the field in San Diego, his first since he went on the injured list in June with a hurt rib. Manager Aaron Boone said Judge could be back during the home stand that starts Tuesday.

items.headline: Padres beat the Yankees 4-3 in San Diego
items.summary: San Diego hit three home runs in a row off Gerrit Cole to start the game Sunday. New York scored three runs in the eighth inning but could not catch up.

items.headline: IUP sweeps Lake Erie for its fourth win in a row
items.summary: The Crimson Hawks won 25-23, 25-16 and 25-14 on Saturday at home. Charlotte Potvin had 11 kills, Delaney Concannon had 15 digs, and IUP is now 5-3.

items.headline: IUP beats Daemen to finish a perfect weekend
items.summary: The Crimson Hawks lost the first set Saturday at home and then won the next three, 25-20, 25-19 and 25-18. They went 4-0 in their own tournament, and Delaney Concannon had 19 kills and 20 digs.

items.headline: Kamara and Cam Jordan may miss the opener
items.summary: Alvin Kamara hurt his knee in an August 18 practice and has not practiced since. Coach Kellen Moore has not ruled out Kamara or defensive end Cam Jordan for Sunday's game at Detroit.

items.headline: Arch Manning throws four touchdown passes
items.summary: Texas opened the season Saturday with a 59-7 win over Texas State in Austin. Manning threw for 305 yards and four touchdowns before he came out of the game in the third quarter.

items.headline: Storms push back Tulane's opener at Duke
items.summary: Bad weather in Durham held up Saturday's game and the stadium was cleared for a while. Kickoff moved from 2:30 to 4:00 our time.

items.headline: Yankees beat the Padres 5-1 in San Diego
items.summary: New York scored four runs in the second inning Saturday and never trailed. Carlos Rodon gave up one run in five innings, and the Yankees are now 81-61.

items.headline: Florida wins big in Jon Sumrall's first game
items.summary: The Gators beat Florida Atlantic 66-21 on Saturday night in a sold-out stadium. Jadan Baugh ran for 160 yards and three touchdowns, and Aaron Philo threw for 275 yards.

items.headline: Texas hosts top-ranked Ohio State on Saturday
items.summary: Arch Manning threw for 305 yards and four touchdowns in the opener, and now Texas gets a rematch with Ohio State in Austin. The Buckeyes beat Texas 14-7 in last year's opening game.

items.headline: Yankees put Trent Grisham on the injured list
items.summary: The center fielder strained his right hamstring Friday night in San Diego and will miss at least 10 days. New York called up Jasson Dominguez from the minors to take his spot.

items.headline: Duke beats Tulane 17-3 in the opener
items.summary: Tulane's offense never got going Saturday at Duke and the Green Wave managed only a field goal. Duke running back Nate Sheppard carried the ball 35 times for 227 yards and two touchdowns.

items.headline: IUP beats Ashland in four sets at home
items.summary: The Crimson Hawks lost the first set 26-24 on Friday and then won the next three. Delaney Concannon had a season-best 20 kills, Jessica Neiman had 18, and IUP is now 4-3.

items.headline: Tyler Shough is the Saints starting quarterback
items.summary: The Saints put out their lineup chart Friday for the opener at Detroit. Tyler Shough is the starter, Spencer Rattler is behind him, and Travis Etienne Jr. and Alvin Kamara are both listed first at running back.

items.headline: IUP sweeps West Liberty to open its home tournament
items.summary: The Crimson Hawks won 25-23, 25-21 and 25-15 on Friday at the Kovalchick Complex. It was their first home match of the year and made their record 3-3.

items.headline: Padres beat the Yankees on a 10th inning home run
items.summary: Luis Campusano hit a two-run home run in the 10th inning Friday night in San Diego and the Padres won 3-2. New York is now four games behind first-place Tampa Bay.

items.headline: Arch Manning signs a trading card deal with Topps
items.summary: Arch Manning agreed to let Topps make his trading cards and sign autographs for them. His first Topps cards will be in the new Bowman football set.

items.headline: Four Texas home games move up a week
items.summary: Texas said four future home games will now be played a week earlier, starting with New Mexico State on August 28, 2027. College football will begin a week sooner from next season on.

items.headline: Florida's opener Saturday is sold out
items.summary: Florida says every seat is taken for the Florida Atlantic game. It is the 19th home game in a row that has sold out.

items.headline: Trevor Goosby will play in Saturday's opener
items.summary: Coach Steve Sarkisian said Thursday that his left tackle is good to go after a bruised knee. Texas will watch how many plays he takes because it will be hot on Saturday afternoon.

items.headline: Saints let go of two hurt players
items.summary: The Saints released running back Devin Neal and pass rusher Michael Heldman, who were both hurt in the preseason. The team paid them for their recovery time, and it can sign them again later.

items.headline: Yankees win in extra innings in Anaheim
items.summary: New York scored five runs with two outs in the 10th inning Wednesday night and beat the Angels 6-3. Cam Schlittler pitched eight innings and gave up just one run.

items.headline: Saints claim a cornerback off waivers
items.summary: New Orleans picked up cornerback Decamerion Richardson from Las Vegas on Wednesday. Safety Lorenzo Styles Jr. went on injured reserve, and wide receiver Kevin Austin Jr. and tight end Treyton Welch joined the practice squad.

items.headline: Aaron Judge could be back next week
items.summary: Manager Aaron Boone said Judge might return on September 8 but would not promise a date. Judge has been out since May 31 with a cracked rib and has started taking batting practice on the field again.

items.headline: Kamara and Cameron Jordan miss practice this week
items.summary: Coach Kellen Moore said Tuesday that running back Alvin Kamara and defensive end Cameron Jordan are not expected to practice this week. Moore said he will know more about them at the end of next week.

items.headline: Yankees beat Angels 7-3
items.summary: New York hit two home runs in a row in the first inning Tuesday night in Anaheim. Spencer Jones and Jazz Chisholm Jr. hit them, and Gerrit Cole gave up one run in five innings.

items.headline: Ryan McMahon comes off the injured list
items.summary: The Yankees put their third baseman back on the roster Tuesday after he hurt his left thumb two weeks ago. Relief pitcher John Schreiber joined the active roster the same day.

items.headline: Saints add two more to the practice squad
items.summary: New Orleans signed wide receiver Cedric Tillman and tight end Stone Smartt on Tuesday. Tillman spent three seasons with Cleveland, and Smartt was with the Jets last season.

items.headline: Florida is healthy going into Saturday's opener
items.summary: Coach Jon Sumrall said Tuesday that the Gators are pretty healthy and almost everyone is ready to play. Walk-on running back Kelvin Jimenez is out for the year, and tight end Evan Chieca is questionable.

items.headline: Florida posts its first lineup chart of the year
items.summary: The Gators listed their starters Monday for Saturday's opener against Florida Atlantic. Aaron Philo is the quarterback and Jadan Baugh is the running back, while three players are still competing for the last spot on the defensive line.

items.headline: Texas picks Gio Spetic as its kicker
items.summary: Coach Steve Sarkisian said Monday that Spetic, who transferred in from Memphis, won the kicking job for Saturday's opener. Mac Chiumento will punt and Ryan Niblett will return kicks again.

items.headline: Two hurt Texas linemen return to practice
items.summary: Left tackle Trevor Goosby and lineman Laurence Seymore both practiced on Monday. Coach Steve Sarkisian said they both looked really good, but he did not say whether they will play Saturday.

items.headline: Aaron Judge could be back in the lineup September 8
items.summary: Manager Aaron Boone said Monday night that Judge might play when the Yankees get home to face Colorado on September 8. Judge has not played since May 31 because of a cracked rib.

items.headline: Daniel Carlson will be the Saints kicker
items.summary: The Saints kept Carlson for the job after he signed only days before the last preseason game. He kicked the 53-yard field goal that beat Dallas, and coach Kellen Moore said Carlson will do a great job.

items.headline: Yankees claim relief pitcher John Schreiber
items.summary: New York claimed the right-hander off waivers from Kansas City on Monday. He got in before the deadline, so he can pitch for the Yankees in the playoffs.

items.headline: Angels beat Yankees 10-1
items.summary: New York made three errors Monday night in Anaheim and lost the first game of the series. Spencer Jones hit a home run for the only Yankees run.

items.headline: Saints claim two linemen off waivers
items.summary: New Orleans added defensive tackle Colby Wooden from the Colts and offensive tackle Mason Murphy from the Bears on Monday. Both had been let go by their old teams in the league-wide cuts on Sunday.

items.headline: Saints sign 12 players to the practice squad
items.summary: New Orleans filled its 12-spot practice squad on Monday, one day after cutting down to 53 players. Running back Zamir White and kicker Charlie Smyth are both back after being let go on Sunday.

items.headline: Aaron Judge travels west as his recovery moves along
items.summary: Manager Aaron Boone said Monday that Judge will go with the team to California and do more work before games. Judge has not played since May 31 with a cracked rib, and hitting against faster pitching is his next step.

items.headline: Saints set their 53-man roster for the season
items.summary: New Orleans got down to the 53 players the league allows on Sunday. The team let go of 19 players and put five more on injured reserve.

items.headline: Devin Neal is out for the season with a hamstring injury
items.summary: The Saints put the running back on injured reserve Sunday, so he will miss the whole season. He hurt the hamstring in August and made it worse in the preseason game at the Rams.

items.headline: Yankees beat Red Sox 16-1 to take the season series
items.summary: Austin Wells hit two home runs in a nine-run eighth inning Sunday at Yankee Stadium. The win gave New York the season series over Boston and a four-game lead for the top wild card spot.

items.headline: Saints let go of kicker Charlie Smyth
items.summary: The Saints waived Smyth on Sunday as they cut the roster down to 53 players. Daniel Carlson, who made the winning kick in the last preseason game, has the job now.

items.headline: Saints release running back Zamir White
items.summary: New Orleans traded for White earlier this month and let him go Sunday before the roster deadline. He ran the ball four times for 23 yards and a touchdown in his one preseason game.

items.headline: Lombard's knee scan comes back clean
items.summary: The scan on George Lombard Jr.'s right knee showed no damage, only some soreness and swelling. Manager Aaron Boone said the rookie shortstop is day to day and should not need the injured list.

items.headline: Yankees bring Luis Gil back to pitch in relief
items.summary: New York called the right-hander up from Triple-A on Sunday and sent Yerry de los Santos down. Gil has been out since April with a sore shoulder and will now work out of the bullpen.

items.headline: IUP beats Wayne State to close the tournament
items.summary: The Crimson Hawks won 24-26, 25-22, 25-22, 25-20 on Saturday in Detroit. Sammy Stephens had a career-best 14 kills and Charlotte Potvin served five aces.

items.headline: Quincy beats IUP in four sets
items.summary: The Crimson Hawks won the first set 25-17 on Saturday morning in Detroit and then lost the next three. Delaney Concannon led IUP with 13 kills and Brooke Kessler had 12 digs.

items.headline: Saints must cut down to 53 players by Sunday
items.summary: The Saints have to go from 90 players to 53 by Sunday. Coach Kellen Moore said a lot of hard decisions come right after Friday's win at Dallas.

items.headline: George Lombard Jr. leaves game with a sore knee
items.summary: The rookie shortstop hurt his right knee on a swing in the second inning Saturday and came out of the game in the fourth. The Yankees said he would have the knee scanned that night.

items.headline: Red Sox shut out Yankees 6-0
items.summary: Boston pitcher Jake Bennett gave up only three hits in six innings Saturday afternoon and New York never scored. It was the first game of a doubleheader at Yankee Stadium.

items.headline: Saints let go of 10 players before Sunday's deadline
items.summary: The Saints released 10 players late Saturday, including receivers Bub Means and Ronnie Bell. The team has to be down to 53 players by 5 p.m. Sunday, so more cuts are still coming.

items.headline: Yankees beat Red Sox 9-2 in the nightcap
items.summary: New York had 13 hits Saturday night and every one of them was a single. Max Fried pitched into the fourth inning in his first game back from the injured list.

items.headline: IUP wins a five-set thriller over Northwood
items.summary: The Crimson Hawks won 25-15, 18-25, 22-25, 25-23, 19-17 on Friday in Detroit for their first win of the season. Their 73 kills were the most the team has had under coach Avery Moore.

items.headline: Sumrall says Florida will not add former pro players
items.summary: Coach Jon Sumrall said Friday that his roster is full and he is not signing anyone who has played pro football. He said that once a player goes pro, that ship has sailed.

items.headline: Saints beat Cowboys 27-24 on a last-minute kick
items.summary: Daniel Carlson made a 53-yard field goal with under a minute left Friday night in Arlington. All three kickers competing for the job kicked in the game, which closed out the preseason.

items.headline: Yankees beat Red Sox 1-0
items.summary: Paul Goldschmidt hit a home run in the third inning Friday night for the game's only run. Cody Bellinger threw a Boston runner out at home plate to end the seventh inning.

items.headline: Max Fried comes off the injured list to pitch Saturday
items.summary: The left-hander will start one game of Saturday's doubleheader against Boston. He has been out since the middle of August with a bruised left elbow.

items.headline: Hillsdale beats IUP in four sets
items.summary: The Crimson Hawks won the first set Friday in Detroit and then lost the next three. Delaney Concannon and Jessica Neiman each had 12 kills, and Elliott Rauch handed out 21 assists.

items.headline: Lombard makes an error in six straight games
items.summary: Rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. made an error in Thursday night's 5-1 loss to Houston. It was his sixth game in a row with one, something no Yankee had done since 1921.

items.headline: Tulane practices on grass to get ready for Duke
items.summary: The Green Wave held their last tune-up practice Friday at the Saints facility so they could work on a real grass field. Duke's stadium has grass, and Tulane opens there on September 5.

items.headline: Three kickers still fighting for the Saints job
items.summary: Tanner Brown made all eight of his field goal tries at Wednesday's practice, while Charlie Smyth and Daniel Carlson each missed one. Coach Kellen Moore says he wants to see them kick in Friday's game at Dallas before he picks one.

items.headline: Findlay beats IUP in the season opener
items.summary: The Crimson Hawks lost in four sets Thursday at Findlay, 27-25, 26-24, 19-25, 25-23. Jessica Neiman led IUP with 12 kills and Delaney Concannon added 9 kills and 12 digs.

items.headline: Astros beat Yankees 5-1 to take the series
items.summary: Christian Walker had three hits and a two-run home run off Gerrit Cole on Thursday night. Houston won two of the three games in the Bronx.

items.headline: Aaron Judge does not want a minor league rehab stint
items.summary: Judge said Thursday he plans to come straight back to the Yankees once doctors clear him. He is still healing a small crack in a rib.

items.headline: Fernando Cruz has a partly torn elbow ligament
items.summary: Manager Aaron Boone said Wednesday that a scan found the tear in the relief pitcher's right elbow. Cruz may need surgery, and he could miss the rest of the season either way.

items.headline: Three Texas freshmen make a national award list
items.summary: Linebacker Tyler Atkinson, receiver Jermaine Bishop Jr. and pass rusher Richard Wesley were named to the watch list for the Shaun Alexander Freshman of the Year Award. Only Alabama, Michigan and Ohio State had as many players on it.

items.headline: Saints will rest starters in Friday game at Dallas
items.summary: Coach Kellen Moore said most of the starters will not play in the last preseason game at Dallas on Friday night. They already got their work in during three joint practices with the Cowboys.

items.headline: Saints add two defensive backs
items.summary: New Orleans signed cornerback Michael Davis and defensive back David Long Jr. on Wednesday. Both are veterans, and the Saints needed help in the secondary after losing cornerback Rejzohn Wright for the season.

items.headline: Yankees beat Astros 9-3
items.summary: Cody Bellinger hit a bases-loaded double in the seventh inning Wednesday night to put New York ahead. Pitcher Elmer Rodriguez had the best start of his career, and the Yankees evened the series.

items.headline: Fernando Cruz goes on the injured list
items.summary: The Yankees put the relief pitcher on the 15-day injured list Wednesday with a sore right elbow. They signed pitcher Michael Fulmer and called up Elmer Rodriguez to take the innings.

items.headline: Chris Olave hurt at practice, coach says it is minor
items.summary: The receiver landed on his back late in Tuesday's practice and had the wind knocked out of him. Coach Kellen Moore said the injury looks minor.

items.headline: Cornerback Rejzohn Wright out for the season
items.summary: Wright hurt his hip and needs surgery. The Saints put him on the injured list, so he will miss the whole season.

items.headline: Two Saints out for the season with knee injuries
items.summary: Running back Ty Chandler and tight end Moliki Matavao were both put on injured reserve Tuesday. Both got hurt in Saturday's game against the Rams, and neither will play again this year.

items.headline: Astros beat Yankees 9-7
items.summary: Yordan Alvarez hit a go-ahead triple in the eighth inning Tuesday night at Yankee Stadium. Cody Bellinger and Luis Garcia Jr. homered for New York, but the bullpen gave up the lead.

items.headline: Zeon Chriss-Gremillion will start at quarterback
items.summary: Coach Will Hall picked Chriss-Gremillion to start Tulane's opener at Duke on September 5. He has started 13 college games, first at Louisiana and then at Houston.

items.headline: Aaron Philo will start at quarterback for Florida
items.summary: Coach Jon Sumrall named Philo his starting quarterback on Monday. Philo transferred in from Georgia Tech and beat out Tramell Jones Jr. for the job.

items.headline: Arch Manning named to Manning Award watch list
items.summary: Forty quarterbacks made the preseason list for the award, which goes to the best quarterback in college football. It is named for Arch's grandfather Archie and his uncles Peyton and Eli.

items.headline: Saints sign kicker Daniel Carlson
items.summary: New Orleans signed kicker Daniel Carlson on Monday. He has been an All-Pro twice and made 22 of his 27 field goal tries last season.

items.headline: Saints trade for running back Zamir White
items.summary: The Saints got running back Zamir White from San Francisco and sent linebacker Deion Jones the other way. They needed help in the backfield with Alvin Kamara and Devin Neal both hurt.

items.headline: Yankees beat Blue Jays 8-3
items.summary: Ben Rice hit a two-run single in the sixth inning on Sunday to break the game open. Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Trent Grisham each hit a home run late as New York won for the sixth time in seven games.

items.headline: Ryan Weathers goes on the injured list
items.summary: The Yankees put the left-handed starter on the 15-day injured list Sunday with a strained muscle in his left forearm. Manager Aaron Boone said Weathers will not throw for two to four weeks but should pitch again this season.

items.headline: Rookie Christen Miller stands out in loss to Rams
items.summary: The second-round pick made three run stops on only eight run-defense snaps in his first preseason game. He was one of the few bright spots in a 34-0 loss.

items.headline: Two quarterbacks lead the way in last scrimmage
items.summary: Kadin Semonza and Zeon Chriss-Gremillion took most of the first-team snaps in Tulane's final scrimmage on Saturday at Yulman Stadium. Coach Will Hall said he will name his starting quarterback on Monday.

items.headline: Nobody hurt in Texas scrimmage, Goosby improving
items.summary: Coach Steve Sarkisian said Texas ran 120 plays on Saturday without a new injury. Left tackle Trevor Goosby is making good progress on his bruised knee, and lineman Laurence Seymore returns to practice Monday.

items.headline: Defense forces four turnovers in Texas scrimmage
items.summary: The Texas defense took the ball away four times in Saturday's practice game in Austin. Arch Manning threw touchdown passes to Ryan Wingo and Emmett Mosley V, and coach Steve Sarkisian said the offense has to stop giving the ball away.

items.headline: Stanton hurts calf, may miss rest of season
items.summary: Giancarlo Stanton strained his left calf while running the bases this week, just as he was finishing his comeback from a right calf injury. Manager Aaron Boone said the team is not ruling anything out, but there is not much season left.

items.headline: Two Longhorns on top defender watch list
items.summary: Rasheem Biles and Colin Simmons were named to the watch list for the Chuck Bednarik Award, which goes to the best defensive player in college football. Both made the list last year too.

items.headline: Three Saints hurt in loss to Rams
items.summary: Running back Devin Neal hurt a hamstring and tight end Moliki Matavao hurt a knee in the first half. Lineman Torricelli Simpkins left the game with a concussion.

items.headline: Rams shut out Saints 34-0
items.summary: The Saints did not score in Saturday's preseason game at Los Angeles. They gave the ball away three times, were called for 12 penalties, and missed their only field goal try.

items.headline: Cody Bellinger back in the lineup Sunday
items.summary: Bellinger said he will play Sunday against Toronto, his first game since he hurt his hamstring on July 25. He is batting .259 with 11 home runs this season.

items.headline: Ryan Weathers leaves game with arm pain
items.summary: The Yankees starter walked off in the fourth inning on Saturday with soreness in his left forearm. He has already pitched more innings this year than in any season of his career.

items.headline: Blue Jays end Yankees' win streak at five
items.summary: Toronto won 4-3 on Saturday afternoon at Yankee Stadium. Nathan Lukes homered in the eighth inning, and a two-run homer by New York in the bottom of the inning was not enough.

items.headline: Myles Graham makes top defender watch list
items.summary: Florida linebacker Myles Graham was named to the watch list for the Bednarik Award, given to college football's best defensive player. He led the Gators with 76 tackles last season.

items.headline: Jack Tchienchou makes top defender watch list
items.summary: Tulane safety Jack Tchienchou was named to the watch list for the Bednarik Award, which goes to the best defensive player in college football. He led Tulane with 83 tackles last season.

items.headline: Linebacker Ty'Anthony Smith leaves Texas
items.summary: Junior linebacker Ty'Anthony Smith is no longer with the Longhorns. Texas loses a veteran at that spot two weeks before its first game.

items.headline: NFL fines Saints $500,000 for practice fights
items.summary: The Saints and Cowboys were each fined after multiple fights broke out during their joint practice in Oxnard on Tuesday. It is one of the largest fines the NFL has issued for a joint practice.

items.headline: Ryan McMahon out with a sprained thumb
items.summary: McMahon sprained his left thumb sliding into second base against Baltimore and went on the 10-day injured list. The Yankees called up Max Schuemann, and McMahon is not expected to be out long.

items.headline: Wilson and Rattler push for backup quarterback job
items.summary: Tyler Shough is the starter, so Zach Wilson and Spencer Rattler are competing to be the backup. Coach Kellen Moore said both are playing good ball, and Saturday's game at the Rams gives each another turn.

items.headline: Yankees beat Blue Jays for fifth win in a row
items.summary: Rookie Spencer Jones hit a two-run home run in the second inning and New York won 3-1 on Friday night. The Yankees are now three games behind Tampa Bay in the American League East.

items.headline: Five Gators make Senior Bowl watch list
items.summary: Kamran James, Eric Singleton Jr., Bryce Thornton, Jadan Baugh and Myles Graham were named to the Senior Bowl's preseason top 300 list. It is an early sign that pro scouts will be watching them this fall.

items.headline: Tulane linebacker makes national comeback list
items.summary: Dickson Agu hurt his knee in September and missed the rest of last season. He is now one of 94 players named to the watch list for college football's Comeback Player of the Year award.

items.headline: LJ McCray up for national comeback award
items.summary: McCray broke his foot early last year and played only four snaps all season. He is back healthy and on the watch list for college football's Comeback Player of the Year award.

items.headline: Arch Manning named to Golden Arm Award watch list
items.summary: For the second year in a row, Texas quarterback Arch Manning made the watch list for the nation's top upperclassman quarterback. It comes as No. 5 Texas looks to bounce back from last year's two early losses and get back into the College Football Playoff.

items.headline: Three Saints leave joint practice early
items.summary: Guard Cesar Ruiz hurt an ankle and did not finish Thursday's practice with the Rams. Lineman John Ridgeway and cornerback Dalys Beanum also left early, and coach Kellen Moore said the team will keep an eye on all three.

items.headline: Aaron Judge nearing his return
items.summary: Judge started hitting off a tee and doing soft toss this week as he recovers from his rib injury. Most reports point to him coming back sometime in September.

items.headline: Gerrit Cole passes Clemens on Yankees K list
items.summary: Cole struck out eight in New York's 6-1 win over Baltimore, moving past Roger Clemens for 12th on the Yankees' all-time strikeout list. It capped a series sweep and the team's fourth straight win.

items.headline: Alvin Kamara out at least a month with knee sprain
items.summary: Kamara sprained the MCL in his knee during Tuesday's joint practice with the Cowboys and is expected to miss at least a month. It's a tough blow to the Saints' offense heading into the season.

items.headline: Goosby could return by season opener
items.summary: Doctors say Trevor Goosby's knee bruise should heal in two to three weeks. That could have him back for the September 5 opener, and he should be ready by the Ohio State game on September 12 at the latest.

items.headline: Yankees trade catcher Christian Bethancourt to Pirates
items.summary: New York sent Bethancourt to Pittsburgh for cash after he hit .333 at Triple-A. The Pirates needed catching depth with their starter out with a hip injury.

items.headline: Stanton nearing return from calf injury
items.summary: Manager Aaron Boone said Giancarlo Stanton is near the end of his running program and responding well. There is still no firm timeline for his return.

items.headline: Yankees edge Orioles in third straight win
items.summary: New York beat Baltimore 5-3 on Wednesday, helped by a controversial call that went the Yankees' way and a home run from Ben Rice. It was the Yankees' third win over the Orioles in a row.

items.headline: Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson out 8 weeks
items.summary: First-round pick Jordyn Tyson strained his hamstring and is expected to miss about eight weeks. Coach Kellen Moore says this injury is not related to his past hamstring problems.

items.headline: Four Longhorns named to preseason All-America team
items.summary: Trevor Goosby, Cam Coleman, Colin Simmons, and Rasheem Biles all made the AP's preseason All-America team, more than any other program in the country. It's a strong vote of confidence heading into the season.

items.headline: Saints, Cowboys scuffle in joint practice
items.summary: Tuesday's joint practice with the Cowboys in Oxnard got chippy, with several scuffles breaking out. Coach Kellen Moore said the team still got the work it needed done.

items.headline: Left tackle Goosby has bone bruise in knee
items.summary: Star left tackle Trevor Goosby was diagnosed with a bone bruise in his left knee after a non-contact injury at Monday's practice. He avoided a torn ligament, but his timeline for returning is still unclear.

items.headline: Carlos Rodón returns with 4 solid innings
items.summary: Rodón made his first start since early July and pitched four innings against Baltimore. Trent Grisham's home run carried the Yankees to a 3-1 win.

items.headline: Max Fried back on IL with elbow bone bruise
items.summary: The Yankees placed Max Fried on the injured list Monday with the same left elbow bone bruise that cost him two months earlier this season. There is no timetable yet for his return.

items.headline: Aaron Judge begins hitting progression
items.summary: Judge will start hitting this week as he works back from the rib fracture that has kept him out since early June. The Yankees are hopeful he can return to the lineup in September.

items.headline: QB battle still even after first scrimmage
items.summary: Neither Aaron Philo nor Tramell Jones Jr. has separated himself in fall camp, coach Jon Sumrall said after Florida's first scrimmage. The competition is expected to continue right up until the season opener.

items.headline: Florida left out of preseason AP Top 25
items.summary: The Gators didn't crack the AP's preseason poll, though they had the second-most votes among unranked teams. It's a fresh-start season under new coach Jon Sumrall, so this is the low point expectations can only rise from.

items.headline: Sumrall gives injury update after scrimmage
items.summary: Receiver Vernell Brown III and defensive back Dijon Johnson, who both sat out the scrimmage as a precaution, were back at full practice Monday. Defensive back Jordy Lowery was the only player actually hurt, with a minor soft-tissue injury.

items.headline: Four quarterbacks still fighting for the job
items.summary: Zeon Chriss-Gremillion ran for two touchdowns in the first fall scrimmage and the offense gave the ball away only once. Coach Will Hall names his first depth chart on August 24.

items.headline: Defense dominates in first fall scrimmage
items.summary: Tulane's defense set the tone early in Saturday's first scrimmage, and coach Will Hall said the offense answered back in the red zone. The four-way quarterback race stays open with the season opener three weeks away.

items.headline: IUP volleyball picked second in its division
items.summary: Coaches picked the Crimson Hawks second in the PSAC West, behind Gannon. IUP went 9-5 in the division last season and brings back three all-conference players.
